reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the opposite. God repeatedly states that He has seen the affliction of the people ('רָאֹה רָאִיתִי אֶת־ עָנְיָ֣ם' - 'I have indeed seen the affliction of My people'), heard their groaning and cries ('וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם' - 'And God heard their groaning'), and knows their sorrows ('יָדַעְתִּי אֶת־ מַכְאֹבָיו' - 'I know their sorrows'). God's motivation is explicitly to deliver the people from Egyptian oppression. The provision of manna and water in the wilderness further demonstrates God's care for the people's material welfare. While God does interact with and direct the leaders (Moses and Aaron), they serve as instruments through which God ministers to the people. The text shows God's empathy is fundamentally directed toward the suffering people, not toward elevating the leaders above them.
